decision: Do not make a narrow ordinary-interpreter source change without a defensible prediction of at least 10% robust full-Windows user-CPU reduction and exact guest parity.

ordinaryWindowsV8.limitation: These V8 self-sample categories are disjoint but are not mode-specific or an estimate of removable work. Step and instruction dispatch include necessary fault/restart, trap, and opcode behavior.

directWindowsExperiment.change: Reuse the per-instruction register/segment snapshot buffer with a reentrancy guard while preserving fault rollback and fresh public snapshots.
directWindowsExperiment.guestParity: Exact after deleting only execution revision and source hashes.
directWindowsExperiment.interpretation: The closest low-risk attack on step overhead was slower on the direct ordinary Windows pair. A 10M GC trace reduced scavenges, but did not establish full-run CPU gain.

otherBoundedEvidence.samePageImmediateFetch: Already in current core; prior xv6 paired user-CPU speedup was about 1.029x, with bytewise boundary fallback.
otherBoundedEvidence.atRamReadShortcut: Prior xv6 full-guest gain about 1.8%; candidate discarded. This is not a Windows timing measurement.
otherBoundedEvidence.inlineMovLeaEa: Prior xv6 ABBA mean gain about 1.3%; candidate discarded. This is not a Windows timing measurement.
otherBoundedEvidence.interruptArbitration: _serviceInterrupts is only 913/66196 (1.38%) of ordinary Windows V8 self-samples. Removing it entirely cannot reach the keep threshold.

structuralFinding: The current fetch path preserves each byte's 15-byte, CS-limit, paging, A20, bus, and partial-EIP fault semantics. Its same-page immediate shortcut is already present. A larger fetch or dispatch shortcut would need cross-mode code/data windows, coherent self-modifying and DMA writes, page-table side effects, precise fault rollback, and chip/IRQ boundaries. No bounded single-function change found in this audit has a credible >=10% whole-Windows CPU prediction. A broad validated multi-instruction path is the next architectural experiment; this note makes no speed claim and adds no emulator code.
